report:
**Conclusion:** Your claim is too strong. The evidence is limited and not definitive, but it leans toward *improved sleep under some conditions* when a window or bedroom door increases ventilation—not that opening either one reliably improves everyone’s sleep.

A 2016 pair of field-intervention experiments in single-occupancy student rooms compared normal ventilation with higher ventilation (via open window or an outdoor-air inlet). Higher ventilation improved some sleep-related measures and perceived air quality, but **did not significantly improve the overall sleep-quality scale or next-day performance**. This is meaningful experimental evidence, but it involved a narrow population and cannot establish a universal effect.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26452168/

A small 2017 observational/within-home study of 17 healthy young adults compared open window or internal door with both closed, measuring CO₂, temperature and humidity over five days and using sleep diaries/questionnaires. It supports the plausible mechanism—opening can lower accumulated CO₂ and alter bedroom conditions—but relies substantially on subjective sleep measures and is too small to be conclusive.  
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/ina.12435

A later field intervention measured 40 Danish bedrooms for two weeks during heating season, specifically testing window/door opening, indoor air quality, sleep and next-day cognition. Its scale and real-home setting add support, but such studies cannot fully separate ventilation from temperature, outdoor noise, light, pollen, pollution, and participants’ expectations.  
https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/a-field-intervention-study-of-the-effects-of-window-and-door-open

A 2020 review emphasizes that bedroom-specific ventilation/sleep evidence remains relatively sparse.  
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360132320306004

So: **reasonable, condition-dependent advice—not a proven general sleep treatment.** If outdoor noise, pollution, allergens, security, or uncomfortable temperature worsen, an open window may hurt rather than help.
